questions.question: Q1 What is the primary purpose of Electrical Die Sorting (EDS) in a semiconductor fab?

answers.a: To physically cut the wafer disk into separate computing chips
answers.b: To test every chip electrically and filter out defective dies before packaging
answers.c: To grow a protective oxide glass insulator over the bare silicon substrate
answers.d: To chemically polish structural blemishes off the back of the wafer disk

explanations.a: Dicing or sawing cuts the wafer into separate pieces, which occurs after testing.
explanations.b: Correct! EDS tests every individual die to ensure functional parts are sent to packaging.
explanations.c: Oxidation layers are grown much earlier in the frontend manufacturing line.
explanations.d: Backside polishing is a physical planarization step, not a logical verification process.

questions.question: Q2 In the virtual lab visualization grid, what do Green and Red color blocks signify?

answers.a: Green shows P-type wells; Red shows N-type source regions
answers.b: Green shows passing chips; Red shows failing or defective chips
answers.c: Green shows copper wires; Red shows aluminum contact lines
answers.d: Green shows high temperature zones; Red shows cryo-cooled points

explanations.a: Doping regions are handled during ion implantation, not electrical die sorting.
explanations.b: Correct! Green blocks identify passing functional dies, while Red labels reject parts.
explanations.c: Wiring metallurgy choices are handled during back-end metallization steps.
explanations.d: The color layout tracks step-by-step test pass/fail results, not thermal gradients.

questions.question: Q3 What happens to the internal transistor gate logic when supply voltage drops too low?

answers.a: The transistors switch states faster, increasing processing performance
answers.b: The transistors cannot switch states fast enough, causing timing path failures
answers.c: The metal wires melt due to immense thermal energy spikes
answers.d: The chip converts automatically into a high-capacity memory storage array

explanations.a: Lower voltages reduce drive current, which slows down transistor switching speeds.
explanations.b: Correct! Under-voltage states create propagation delays, leading to chip failures.
explanations.c: Melting occurs due to high current overloads, which is associated with over-voltage.
explanations.d: Physical transistor configurations cannot transform logic structures into memory arrays.

questions.question: Q4 How is the manufacturing Yield Percentage mathematically calculated?

answers.c: Total Passing Dies multiplied by the Test Frequency value
answers.d: Supply Voltage divided by the total number of Red failing blocks

explanations.a: This fraction is inverted and would mathematically produce values greater than 100%.
explanations.b: Correct! Yield percentage measures the passing dies divided by total fabricated dies.
explanations.c: Yield is an efficiency ratio, not a function of raw frequency values.
explanations.d: This does not match any valid semiconductor manufacturing or efficiency metric.

questions.question: Q5 What hardware interface connects the automated testing unit to the tiny metal pads on a chip?

answers.d: An Anisotropic Plasma Gas Injector Nozzle

explanations.a: Sputter targets are used to supply raw metal atoms inside PVD chambers.
explanations.b: Correct! Probe cards use micro-needles to establish electrical contact with the wafer pads.
explanations.c: Linear accelerator columns are used to speed up ions during implantation.
explanations.d: Gas nozzles feed reactive chemical ions into dry plasma etching configurations.

questions.question: Q6 Which phase of semiconductor fabrication deals with checking and sorting dies before final assembly?

explanations.a: FEOL deals with making raw components inside the silicon, not late-stage sort checks.
explanations.b: Correct! Late-stage probing and filtering fall under BEOL sorting pipelines.
explanations.c: Ingot pulling runs during standard raw baseline substrate preparation steps.
explanations.d: Planarization is a physical flattening process, not an electrical sanity test.

questions.question: Q7 What are the two primary parameters tweaked by the operator during this sorting simulation?

explanations.a: Gas dynamics apply to gas processing chambers, not die sort probing beds.
explanations.b: Correct! Voltage and frequency controls act as your core testing stress rules.
explanations.c: Etch time matches processing setups, while ion values define doping profiles.
explanations.d: Beam parameters belong to ion implantation and lithography sub-consoles.

questions.question: Q8 What historic method was used to tag a broken die on a physical wafer before software mapping tools?

answers.a: Laser-cutting a visible alignment hole directly through the silicon layer
answers.b: Dropping a physical dot of specialized magnetic ink onto the die surface
answers.c: Baking the substrate inside a high-temperature structural anneal furnace
answers.d: Scratching the active pattern layer using sharp diamond tip tweezers

explanations.a: Laser cutting creates internal physical fractures that destroy neighboring dies.
explanations.b: Correct! Legacy probers used physical ink drop heads to flag bad parts.
explanations.c: Furnace steps run to repair crystal damage, not mark test errors.
explanations.d: Manual scraping introduces contamination and unpredictable crystal fractures.

questions.question: Q9 Which term represents the metric for computational speed checks forced onto a die?

explanations.a: Sheet resistance handles electrical attributes following ion doping steps.
explanations.b: Correct! Test frequency dictates clock cycle rules per second during check routines.
explanations.c: Thickness definitions govern physical depth profiles during mask or wiring steps.
explanations.d: Thermal tracking parameters handle cooling limits, not clock cycles.

questions.question: Q10 Why does testing a die at the wafer level provide an immense business advantage?

answers.a: It chemically transforms standard silicon to make its gates switch faster
answers.b: It avoids wasting money on final packaging materials for defective chips
answers.c: It bypasses the need for costly photolithography masking sequences
answers.d: It automatically bridges open circuits and repairs bad metallization lines

explanations.a: Electrical sort testing checks functional criteria; it cannot alter chemical compositions.
explanations.b: Correct! Screening parts early prevents high downstream packaging expenses on scrap elements.
explanations.c: Mask layouts are required to set up the circuit baseline architecture beforehand.
explanations.d: Testing evaluates operating telemetry; it does not repair layout cracks or faults.
